messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming-p99 > 2.0s for /v1/stream (region=eu). paging @mia (oncall) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: p95=520ms p99=2200ms error-rate up 0.8% client timeouts rising :warning:
mia (oncall): on it, queuing context + joining call now
mia (oncall): raj can you dump the proxy tail and recent traces for a sample request?
raj: grabbing traces now. seeing a pattern: long write delays to client sockets, proxy write queue growing
olivia: seeing a spike in upstream latency too around same window, but origin model latencies look normal for non-stream endpoints
samir: could be slow consumers/backpressure at the SSE connection level. any socket fd saturation on edge?
edge-bot: recent logs snippet for proxy-03 (eu-west-1):
```
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z WARN write: client_write_timeout=120s chunk_buffer=4096 queued=78
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z INFO conn=0x7f3a wrote 0 bytes, backpressure=true
2026-03-15T10:02:13Z ERROR upstream write error: EAGAIN
```
raj: looks like proxy queuing at the ALB->proxy layer, some clients are slow to read chunks. p99 stalls map to those queued connections
ben (platform): any recent deploys to streaming proxy or LB?
olivia: no code deploys in last 6h. config change: routing policy to prefer compressed-chunk variant rolled out 1h ago (auto).
samir: compressed-chunk increases payload density but can aggravate slow consumer stalls if client buffers are small. might be interacting with client/browser backpressure
cs-ops: we have 3 paying customers reporting partial transcript delays, ~7% of streams delayed >5s. raising CS priority.
mia (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) revert compressed-chunk routing 2) increase proxy write concurrency / reduce chunk size 3) enable circuit-break for stuck connections (drop after Xs) 4) route new streams to dedicated low-batch variant
raj: quick check - we can flip routing rule to prefer non-compressed small-chunk variant (model-v1-small-chunk) at the edge feature-flag level. takes ~30s to roll
ben (platform): I can flip flag and watch. prepping runbook command
ben (platform): running: `infrctl feature-flag set streaming.prefer_small_chunks=true --region eu-west-1`
ben (platform): ✅ flag updated, starting gradual roll 10% -> 100% over 2min
olivia: observing immediate drop in queued connections on proxy-03
edge-bot: metric update (after 60s): queued=12 p99=1150ms p95=430ms
samir: good sign. but we should also tighten proxy write timeout so stuck sockets don't hold resources
ben (platform): updating proxy config: `proxy.write_timeout=30s` and `chunk_size=1024` for eu cluster
ben (platform): apply rolling restart to proxies (controlled)
raj: rolling restarts show per-host drains - watch for reconnect storm. enabling gradual drain and 30s grace
mia (oncall): CS-ops please notify the impacted customers we've applied mitigations and we're monitoring. include ETA for full recovery ~15-30m
cs-ops: sending note now. will post copy here when sent
cs-ops: sent to customers A,B,C: "We've detected intermittent streaming delays affecting a subset of sessions in EU. We're rolling a fix to prefer small-chunk streams and reduce proxy write timeouts. Monitoring closely. Will update in 15m."
olivia: retention of KV cache looks fine; not related. model runtime cpu is stable. this is mostly in edge/proxy backpressure
edge-bot: after restart wave: p95=300ms p99=540ms queued=4 error-rate back to baseline
mia (oncall): marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. need root cause: interaction between compressed-chunk routing + slow browser consumers + default long write timeout.
samir: action items: - (1) full traffic replay + load test with slow-reader clients to reproduce - (2) revert compressed-chunk default until we have graceful backpressure logic - (3) add socket-level metrics per-client-window - (4) postmortem doc and ETA to CS
raj: I'll attach trace examples and the `tcpdump`/proxy logs to the incident ticket
ben (platform): I'll open a follow-up to add an automated fallback: if proxy queued connections > threshold, switch routing to small-chunk variant automatically
mia (oncall): nice. I'll create the incident page and assign owners: raj for logs/traces, samir for reproducer & load test, ben for auto-fallback, olivia for config audit, cs-ops for customer comms
mia (oncall): oncall handoff: I'm staying on for 45m to watch metrics, then will hand to next oncall (tomorrow morning) with full notes
incident-bot: NOTE: added incident tag streaming-eu-2026-03-15 to ticket #INC-4821
cs-ops: if anything customer-facing changes, ping me and I'll update the active messages
olivia: small follow: increase in slow consumer cases seems correlated with a third-party CDN change for a subset of customers. reaching out to partner contact
samir: adding a quick reproducer script for slow-reader here:
```
# slow-reader curl simulate
mkfifo /tmp/f; (head -c 1024 /dev/zero > /tmp/f &) ; curl --no-buffer http://edge-eu/v1/stream | pv -qL 100
```
mia (oncall): thanks team. leaving timeline and notes in the incident doc. next update in 30m or earlier if regression
cs-ops: customers acknowledged. some lowered severity after our mitigation :thumbsup:
mia (oncall): closing on-call page for active mitigation, keeping incident open for postmortem track. handoff scheduled to @raj for morning follow-up
